copy: 1.3 billion people live with a serious disability. If your body did everything you asked of it today, don't take that for granted.
3.4 billion people on Earth don't have a safe toilet, and unsafe waste spreads disease. If yours flushes and you never think about it, be grateful.
The 8-hour workday only became law in 1919. Before that, 60-hour weeks were normal everywhere. If you clock off tonight, someone fought for that. Be grateful.
560 million people get electricity from a solar panel because no power line reaches them. If you can see a working wall outlet right now, be grateful.
3.7 billion people live with untreated tooth decay. If you ate today without a flash of pain, don't take that for granted.
Last year, 14.7 million people who had been forced from their homes finally got to go back. If you never had to leave yours, be grateful.
The power grid stretches 80 million kilometers — a hundred trips to the moon. If there's an outlet in your wall, that's where it ends.
1 in 12 men can't see the full range of color. If this morning's sky showed you every shade, don't take that for granted.
In 1820, 8 in 10 humans lived in extreme poverty. Today it's fewer than 1 in 10. You were born into the richest moment in history. Be grateful for it.
2.5 billion people need glasses, a hearing aid, or a wheelchair they don't have. If the ones you need simply arrived — or your body needs none — be grateful.
In 7 of 10 homes without running water, it's women and girls who walk to fetch the water. A kitchen tap hands those hours back, every day.
In 1820, only 1 in 10 adults could read. You're reading this right now. Be grateful someone taught you.
96% of the world sits under a mobile signal, but 1 in 4 people can't afford to use it. If you're online right now, be grateful.

statLine: >99% of intercontinental data goes by sea
copy: 99% of the world's internet travels through cables on the ocean floor. If your last message crossed an ocean, it went by sea — and arrived in an instant.
739 million adults can't read a street sign or a medicine label. If you can read this, someone gave you a key to the world. Be grateful.
For nearly all of human history, almost no one could read. You're doing it right now, without even trying. Don't take that for granted.
11,000 working satellites are flying over your head right now. You'll never see a single one, and you use them all day. Be grateful.
4.6 billion people can't get basic health care. If there's a doctor you can reach today, you have what most of the world doesn't. Be grateful.
In medieval Europe, murder was 10 to 70 times more common than it is there today. If you walked somewhere today without a second thought, be grateful.
statLine: Murder: down 10–70x since medieval times · Europe

copy: 73% of people around the world now say they feel safe walking alone at night — the highest ever recorded. If your evening walk feels boring, be grateful.
2 billion cups of coffee are poured around the world every day. If you had one today, a dozen pairs of hands touched it first. Be grateful for them.

statLine: 1 in 11 can't heat their home · EU
copy: Even in wealthy Europe, 1 in 11 people can't afford to keep their home warm. If your thermostat just works, don't take that warmth for granted.
1.16 million people die on the world's roads every year. If you made it home today without a second thought, don't take that for granted.

statLine: Disaster deaths down 90% in a century
copy: A century ago, natural disasters killed a million people in a bad year. Now it's around 15,000 — down 90% while the population quadrupled. The forecast on your phone did that.
As recently as 1988, polio was still paralyzing 350,000 people a year. Today it's nearly gone — and you never had to think about it once. Be grateful.
Nearly 1 in 5 people on Earth has no phone of any kind. If there's one in your pocket right now, don't take it for granted.

statLine: 80M need a wheelchair; most lack one
copy: 80 million people around the world need a wheelchair, and most will never get one. If you can move freely, be grateful for it.
936 million adults have sleep apnea — their breathing stops over and over in the night — and most don't even know it. If you woke up rested this morning, be grateful for it.
117 million people can't sleep in their own home tonight — forced out by war or disaster. Be grateful.
scale: close to the entire population of Japan

copy: 666 million people around the world live without electricity. Be grateful.
scale: nearly every person in the United States, twice

copy: 826 million people can't read up close because they have never owned reading glasses. If you're reading this easily, be grateful.
3.1 billion people around the world live with headache disorders. If your head is clear right now, billions are wishing for a day like yours.
scale: about China, India, and the United States combined

copy: 619 million people lived with back pain last year. If you got out of bed this morning without wincing, don't take that for granted.
1 in 3 adults will struggle to sleep this year. If your nights come easy, don't take them for granted.
2.1 billion people around the world cook over open fires, breathing the smoke. If you cooked on a clean stove today, a quarter of the planet couldn't.
2.6 billion people can't afford a healthy diet. If you ate what you wanted today instead of only what you could afford, be grateful.
Heat kills 489,000 people around the world every year. If you can step into shade or pour cold water right now, don't take that for granted.

statLine: Ozone layer on track to recover ~2040
copy: The ozone layer above you is healing and should fully recover by 2040. The whole world teamed up to fix it in your lifetime. Be grateful for that.
1 billion people are losing their sight from problems doctors already know how to fix. If glasses or an eye doctor were there when you needed them, be grateful.
15% of the world's babies never get their basic vaccines. If you got yours, someone protected you before you could even ask. Be grateful.
Airlines carry 4.7 billion passengers a year, and most people on Earth still aren't one of them. If you fly, be grateful.

statLine: 4 in 5 have never flown · industry estimate
copy: 8 out of 10 people on Earth have never been on an airplane. You've seen what most of the world never will. Be grateful.
scale: more than Asia and Africa combined

copy: 92 million people live at risk of trachoma, an infection that slowly blinds. It spreads where clean water is scarce. If you can wash your face whenever you want, you will almost certainly never get it. Be grateful.
430 million people around the world can't hear well enough to follow a conversation. If you heard your name called today, be grateful.
scale: more than every person in the United States

copy: 1.1 billion people live with sight loss, and 9 out of 10 cases could have been prevented or cured. If you can see this clearly, your eyes never failed you — or someone fixed them. Be grateful either way.
scale: about 3 times the population of the United States

statLine: Air pollution death rate nearly halved since 1990
copy: The death rate from air pollution has been cut in half since 1990. Billions now breathe safer air than their grandparents did. Be grateful.
2.2 billion people around the world can't see clearly. Be grateful.
scale: about the population of China and Europe, combined

copy: GPS is free for everyone on Earth. If your phone can guide you home right now, be grateful for it.

statLine: Tea: the world's most shared drink
copy: After water, tea is the most popular drink on Earth. Whatever's in your cup right now, billions share that same small comfort with you today.

statLine: 1940: half of US homes lacked plumbing · US
copy: As recently as 1940, half of American homes had no indoor plumbing. If hot water just arrives when you turn a tap, be grateful — that's one lifetime old.
2.8 billion people around the world lack adequate housing. 300 million have no home at all. If there's a roof over you tonight, be grateful.
scale: about the population of China and India, combined

copy: 2.2 billion people have never once been online. If you're reading this, you have what a quarter of the planet can't get. Be grateful.
2.1 billion people risk going broke every time they get sick. If you can see a doctor without doing that math, be grateful.
1 in 3 workers around the world puts in over 48 hours a week. If tonight is yours to spend however you want, don't take it for granted.
1 billion people face deadly heat with no fan, no fridge, no cold water. If there's ice in your freezer right now, most of the world can't say that.
304 million people live far from the country they were born in. If the people you love are a short drive away, be grateful.
Your seat-belt cuts your risk of dying in a crash by half. 1.16 million people still die on roads every year. Click it, and be grateful someone invented it.
Since 2000, 2.2 billion people got safe water at home for the very first time. If yours has always been there, you were born lucky.

statLine: 1 in 9 sickened by food each year
copy: 866 million people around the world get sick from their food every year. If your last meal never worried you, be grateful.
In the late 1800s, people worked 3,000 hours a year — by July they had done your whole year. If your evenings and weekends are yours, be grateful.

statLine: 42% of households own a bicycle · 2015 study
copy: Fewer than half the homes on Earth own even a bicycle. If you can get anywhere faster than your own two feet, be grateful.
As recently as 2000, measles killed 780,000 people a year. Last year: 95,000 — vaccines did that. If you got your shots as a kid, you never had to fear it. Be grateful.
For 3,000 years, smallpox killed 3 out of every 10 people it touched. We only wiped it out in 1980. You'll never have to fear it.
1.12 billion people live in slums without power, plumbing, or running water. If your room is dry and warm tonight, be grateful for it.
As recently as 1998, 1 in 4 people on Earth had no electricity. That wasn't very long ago. If your evenings have always been lit, there are billions who can't say the same. Don't forget it.
1 in 8 people lives beyond any road that works year-round — rain can trap them at home for days. If you can always get out, be grateful.
As recently as 2000, 246 million children worked instead of going to school. It's 138 million now — still 1 in 17. If your childhood had a classroom, be grateful.
Since 2015, 310 million people turned on a light in their home for the very first time. If you never had to wait for that day, be grateful.
150 million children under five have never been registered — no legal proof they exist. If you have a birth certificate, don't take that paper for granted.
2.3 billion people can't count on their next meal. If you know exactly where yours is coming from, don't take that for granted.

Half the people on Earth who need cataract surgery will never get it. Cataracts slowly cloud your eyes as you age, and a 10-minute operation clears them. If that operation would be there for you, be grateful.
Today's 5-day weather forecast is as accurate as a 3-day forecast was in 2001. You get to see further ahead than anyone before you.
3.8 billion people have no safety net at all — no pension, no sick pay, no unemployment help. If a system would catch you if you fell, be grateful.
1 in 12 people on Earth has no electricity at all. If your home has power right now, you have what 666 million people are still waiting for.
2.1 billion people around the world can't safely drink the water in their own home. Be grateful.
scale: about the population of China and Europe, combined

copy: As recently as 1990, calling another country cost $2 a minute. Today you can video-call the other side of the planet for free. Don't take that for granted.

statLine: 1.7B without soap and water at home
copy: 1.7 billion people around the world have no soap and water at home — making infections far more likely. If you do, don't take that sink for granted.
1 in 6 people on Earth is lonely. If someone would notice you were gone by tonight, you have real wealth. Don't take them for granted.
As recently as 2000, 1 in 3 young women had been married as children. Today it's under 1 in 5 — and falling. If your childhood was yours, be grateful.
In the World Wars, conflict killed millions of people a year. Today about 1 in 700 deaths comes from war. If your home is at peace, don't take it for granted.
For most of human history, 1 in 2 children died young. Today, 96 out of 100 grow up. Be grateful for every child you know.
There's only 1 car for every 8 people on Earth. If you drove somewhere today, most of the world walked. Be grateful.
In the early 1800s, fewer than 1 in 5 adults had any schooling. Today more than 4 in 5 do. If someone taught you, be grateful.
3 out of 4 homes on Earth have no air conditioning. If you slept in a cool room last night, that's a luxury most people will never feel.
1.7 billion people get medical care in clinics with no running water, where even the doctor can't wash their hands. If yours can, be grateful.
125 million people around the world make their living from coffee. If coffee started your morning, someone's livelihood is in that cup.
In one generation, fire deaths in the US fell 66% — smoke alarms did most of that. Press the test button on yours, and be grateful for the beep.
Every day, 334,000 people get electricity for the very first time in their lives. If you were born with it, don't take that for granted.
5 out of every 7 people on Earth wash their clothes by hand. If a machine does yours, be grateful for the hours it gives back.
852 million adults around the world live with insomnia. If you fell asleep easily last night, 1 in 6 adults lies awake wishing for that. Be grateful.
Vaccines have saved 154 million lives around the world in 50 years. There's a real chance one of them is yours. Be grateful.

statLine: 2 of 3 lack needed glasses · low-income countries
copy: In poorer countries, 2 out of 3 people who need glasses never get a pair. If yours are sitting on your face right now, be grateful for them.
106 million people still drink from rivers and ponds, water that can carry disease. If yours was cleaned, tested and piped straight to you — be grateful.
830 million people have diabetes, and more than half get no medicine for it. If your body keeps your blood sugar steady without you ever thinking about it, be grateful.
1 in 5 people on Earth has no refrigerator at all. Be grateful.
As recently as 2018, only 11% of the world flew anywhere — and just 4% ever crossed a border by air. If travel is normal to you, it isn't to most people.
4 in 5 of the world's elderly now receive a pension — for most of history, almost none did. If your grandparents get that monthly deposit, be grateful.
5 billion people can't get safe surgery when they need it. If an operating room is there for you, you have what most of the world doesn't.
In 1900, the average person lived to 32. You'll likely see more than double that. Be grateful for every extra decade.

statLine: 2.9M killed by cooking smoke a year
copy: Cooking-fire smoke kills 2.9 million people around the world every year. If the air in your kitchen stayed clear tonight, don't take it for granted.
466 million children get their most reliable meal of the day at school. If dinner at home was a guarantee growing up, be grateful.
Leaded gasoline poisoned the air for nearly a century. In 2021 the last country finally banned it. Every breath you take now is cleaner for it.
Since 2000, 2.8 billion people got a safe toilet for the very first time. Yours always just worked. Be grateful.
As recently as 2011, half the adults on Earth had no bank account. If your money moves with a tap, don't take that for granted.
673 million people around the world went hungry last year. If you've never had to plan your day around finding food, be grateful.
